AGENDA
  Old Town La Verne Business Improvement District
  Advisory Board

  Monday, May 5, 2025 – 8:30 am
  2316 D Street – Café Wang

1. WELCOME AND CALL TO ORDER-

  Board Members  City Representatives/Others Present
  Craig Walters, Chair  Eric Scherer, Com. Dev. Director
  George Henderson, Vice Chair  Natalie Hiatt, Com. Dev. Admin. Secretary
  Micky Rehm  Danny Wu, Public Works Director
  Nicole Houston, Senior Management
  Marianne Stark, Treasurer  Analyst
  Zuhey Espinoza

2. CALENDAR-
  Annual Report to City Council  Monday, May 19th 6:30pm

3. APPROVAL OF MINUTES  March 3, 2025 and April 7, 2025

4. NEW BUSINESS
  A.  Introduction of Danny Wu, Public Works Director
  B.  District/Association Bylaws

5. CONTINUED BUSINESS
  A.  Cool Cruise Recap
  B.  Wine Walk Recap

6. COMMITTEE REPORTS/ UPDATES
  A.  City Report (Eric Scherer):
  B.  University Report (Zuhey Espinoza):
  C.  Marketing (Micky Rehm):
  D.  Chamber Report:
  E.  Social Media Update (Micky Rehm):
  F.  Financial Report:

7. PUBLIC COMMENT
  Any discussion or action on non-agendized items must be deferred to the following meeting, as required by law.

8. ADJOURNMENT –  Monday, June 2, 2025, at 8:30 am at Café Wang
  2316 D Street, La Verne CA 91750
   OLD TOWN LA VERNE BUSINESS IMPROVEMENT DISTIRICT
  MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  Monday, March 3, 2025

1.  WELCOME AND CALL TO ORDER

  The meeting began at 8:33 a.m.

  Chairperson Craig Walters welcomed attendees. The following board members were
  present: Chair Craig Walters, Micky Rehm, and George Henderson. Not Present:
  Marianne Stark and Zuhey Espinoza. City representatives present: Councilmember Steve
  Johnson, City Manager Ken Domer, and Community Development Director Eric Scherer.
  Others present: Marlene Carney, Randy Sharp, and Ken Valmonte.

2.  CALENDAR

  Cool Cruise Car Show – Saturday, April 19, 2025 – 10am-4pm
  Wine Walk – Saturday, April 26, 2025 – 5pm-8:30pm

3.  NEW BUSINESS

  La Verne Walk of Fame

  Chair Walters presented the concept of a sidewalk plaque program on D Street to
  recognize those who have contributed to the City. A separate non-profit would be formed
  to solicit donations for the program. The hope is that the first year there could be 20
  people recognized. A QR code would be used to directly link to a website that had more
  information about those who are honored. City Manager Domer mentioned that a
  Community Foundation would be helpful to help organize this and other non-profits in
  the City. It was moved by Henderson, seconded by Rehm to support the concept. Motion
  carried by a 3-0 vote.

  Budget Subcommittee

  Mr. Scherer asked that two member be selected for the Budget subcommittee. It was
  moved by Henderson, seconded by Walters to select Walters and Rehm to the
  subcommittee. Motion carried by a 3-0 vote.

4.  CONTINUED BUSINESS

  Final 5-year Plan Review
   Mr. Scherer presented the Board with the final version of the 5-year plan for the Board’s
  recommendation to the Council that they receive and file the plan. The Board provided
  general support of the plan to move forward without a formal vote.

  Wine Walk Update

  Ms. Rehm mentioned that they were still looking for sponsors, and that the food vendors
  were mostly set. Chair Walters indicated that there would be early-bird pricing on the
  website. City Manager Domer mentioned that it would be a good opportunity to have
  students from the University help with the event. City Manager Domer indicated that the
  Association would be charged up to $3,000 for City staff for the event.

5.  COMMITTEE REPORTS/UPDATES

  A. City Report (Eric Scherer): None

  B. University Report (Zuhey Espinoza): AVP of Facilities Randy Sharp indicated that
  the track was being resurfaced and expected to be completed by July 11th. He also
  mentioned the Gala event will be on May 3rd and that commencement is on May 31st.

  C. Marketing (Micky Rehm): None

  D. Chamber Report (Marlene Carney): Ms. Carney said that she looks forward to
  working with Association on potentially sharing staff and that the Community Yard
  Sale will be held the same day as the Wine Walk on April 26th at Bonita High School.

  E. Social Media Update (Micky Rehm): None.

  F. Financial Report: None

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT (Any discussion or action on non-agendized items must be
  deferred to the following meeting, as required by California Brown Act Law)

  None

7.  ADJOURNMENT

  Meeting was adjourned at 9:24 a.m., the next regular meeting to be held on Monday,
  April 7, 2025 at 8:30 a.m. at Café Wang Restaurant.

  Respectively submitted,

  _____________________
  Eric Scherer
   OLD TOWN LA VERNE BUSINESS IMPROVEMENT DISTIRICT
  MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  Monday, April 7, 2025

1.  WELCOME AND CALL TO ORDER

  Chairperson Walters called the meeting to order at 8:36 a.m. The following Board
  Members were present: Craig Walters, Marianne Stark, Micky Rehm, and George
  Henderson. The following Board Members were absent: Zuhey Espinoza. City
  Representatives present: Mayor Tim Hepburn, Community Development Director Eric
  Scherer and Secretary Natalie Hiatt. Others present: Wendy Norton, Lori Alvarez, Ken
  Valmonte, Marlene Carney and Fang Wang.

2.  CALENDAR
  Cool Cruise  Saturday, April 19th 10am-4pm
  Wine Walk  Saturday, April 26th 5pm-8:30pm

3.  APPROVAL OF THE MINUTES

  None

4.  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Budget Review – Mr. Scherer met with Ms. Rehm and Mr. Walters two weeks
  ago to review the BID Budget. Mr. Scherer discussed the approximate $110,000
  in reserves going directly to the Association to cover the approximate $70,000 in
  events and $40,000 salary for a new staff member shared with the Chamber. The
  $20,000 in expenditure would remain with the City for things such as the annual
  meeting cost, lights, etc. The current car show agreement will expire after the
  Cool Cruise event. The new contract will be negotiated by the Association if they
  continue with the current promoter.

  The Board had questions regarding a shared Chamber and Association employee.
  They also discussed revising the current bylaws. They will have further discussion
  and prepare a proposal for City Council.

  It was moved by Mr. Henderson and seconded by Ms. Rehm to recommend
  approval of the proposed budget. The motion was approved 3-0 (Ms. Stark
  abstained).

  B.  Street Light Banners – Mr. Scherer received an estimate from Public Works for
  the 27 acorn lights in the Old Town. The one banner bracket costs $128/each and
  the two banner bracket cost $184/each. Ms. Rehm received a quote from Courier
  Printing at $42/each for the banner and $65/each for printing. Mr. Scherer
  recommended going over budget this fiscal year and purchasing all the brackets
  and waiting until July 2025 to purchase the banners. The Board agreed to move
   forward with the purchase of all the brackets in preparation for the Gold Line
  opening in August.

5.  CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A.  Wine Walk Update – To be discussed further at the Wine Walk meeting following
  the BID meeting.

6.  COMMITTEE REPORTS/ UPDATES

  A. City Report (Eric Scherer): None.
  B. University Report (Zuhey Espinoza): None.
  C. Marketing (Micky Rehm): None.
  D. Chamber Report: Ms. Carney asked the businesses to notify the Chamber of
  promotions.
  E. Social Media Update (Micky Rehm): None.
  F. Financial Report: None.

7.  PUBLIC COMMENT (Any discussion or action on non-agendized items must be
  deferred to the following meeting, as required by California Brown Act Law)

8.  ADJOURNMENT

  Meeting was adjourned at 9:12 a.m., the regular meeting to be held on May 5, 2025 at
  8:30 a.m. at Café Wang – 2316 D Street, La Verne CA 91750

  Respectively submitted,

  _____________________
  Natalie Hiatt

  the Chamber of commerce and Association are meeting with city staff on May 6,

5  CONTINUED BUSINESS
  A.  Cool Cruise Recap - Mr. Scherer stated that it was a beautiful day. Mr. Scherer
  estimated 40-50 more cars participated.
  B.  Wine Walk Recap - Ms. Rehm stated that the attendance was down due to the
  rain. Ms. Rehm estimated that the profit is approximately $17,000. Ms. Rehm
  received feedback from the attendees that the tickets were too expensive and there
  are too many calendar conflicts that weekend.

  Ms. Houston recommended using a wholesaler that allowed them to return the
  unused wine.
   Mr. Scherer stated that the Association will need to decide on a donation amount
  for La Verne Little League. The presentation of the check will take place at the
  May 19ft City Council meeting.
